body:
Triage (first-touch grading): graded — `finding` → `pm:blocked`, `domain:engine`, type Task.

Blocked-by: #11635

Rationale: the card's own ordering claim is confirmed by the standing record — the boolean-aggregand contract on the PG face is now carried by #11635 (the ruled `false`/`true` + arithmetic answers are unproducible on PG until the lowering cast lands; the same shared-damage direction was already adjudicated when #11152 was re-pointed at it). Converting this suite to the live-dialect matrix before #11635 lands a red on `main` for a reason the conversion did not introduce.

Unlock-action, pre-written: when #11635 closes, re-verify on the merged ref (the cast fix may have converted this suite as part of its own proof — absorb-close if so), then requeue with the deliverable: route `sql-driver-aggregation-conformance.test.ts` through `live-dialect-matrix.testkit.ts` per ADR-0053 D-A3 (`Postgres at minimum`), with the per-dialect readback readings the card names (`pg` returns count as strings — `Number(r.n)` coercion needs a per-dialect face, not a mechanical port).

## ⭐ Unblocked — and the unlock action's own warning was checked, not assumed

`Blocked-by: #11635` is **discharged**: #11635 closed when PR #11785 merged (verified by content — `castBooleanAggregand` 2 on `origin/main`, control `booleanFields` 12, `main` tip *is* the squash commit).

Triage's pre-written unlock action (`5400911981`) attached a condition most unlock scans skip:

> re-verify on the merged ref (**the cast fix may have converted this suite as part of its own proof — absorb-close if so**), then requeue

⇒ **Re-verified on the merged ref. It was NOT absorbed** — so this card is real work, not a stale ticket:

```
client: 'better-sqlite3'   @ origin/main …aggregation-conformance.test.ts:112   → still hard-coded
live-dialect-matrix / DIALECT_CELLS / declareDialectCell                        → ZERO hits
CONTROL: file present and 217 lines                                             → reachable
```

⚠️ Had it been absorbed, the honest disposition was to close it, and the cost of skipping that check is a whole dev cycle spent re-doing work that already landed. ⛔ This is exactly the "the merge that closed your upstream is the most likely thing to have also fixed your card" case.

## The deliverable, from triage verbatim

> route `sql-driver-aggregation-conformance.test.ts` through `live-dialect-matrix.testkit.ts` per ADR-0053 D-A3 (`Postgres at minimum`), with the per-dialect readback readings the card names (`pg` returns count as strings — `Number(r.n)` coercion needs a per-dialect face, **not a mechanical port**)

⚠️ "Not a mechanical port" is the load-bearing clause. #11785 landed the boolean-aggregand answers **hours ago**, so the exact values this suite will now see on PG/MySQL are fresh — re-measure them, ⛔ do not port SQLite's expectations across.

## Premise note

The card was filed as a `finding` and graded to `pm:blocked` by triage; nothing in it has been re-scoped since. Sync `origin/main` before starting — `sql-driver.ts` moved substantially today (#11785, #11868 upstream).

## ACCEPT — PR #12023

Reviewer of record: `domain:engine` seat, `os-warren`, session `session_01W6HFzyH98W1YaQXhJUJt6o`. ⛔ Landing held — last section.

### ⭐ The dispatch's one hard instruction was "not a mechanical port", and the measurement changed the answer

I warned that #11785 had just moved what boolean aggregands answer, so the per-dialect values had to be **re-measured, not ported**. The dev went further and **falsified the obvious reading**:

> the divergent cell is **pg ALONE**, not "the live cells" — mysql2 returns the same BIGINT as a JS number — and within pg it is **not uniform either** (`count` is a string, `sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max` over the float `score` column are numbers), so the coercion is **unconditional** rather than switched on `cell.id` or `cell.live`.

⇒ The intuitive port — branch on "is this a live cell?" — would have been **wrong in both directions**: wrong for MySQL, which needs no coercion, and wrong inside pg, which needs it on one function and not the others. That distinction only exists because someone measured instead of generalising.

### The two per-dialect faces, and why neither is a relaxation

| Case | What was wrong | What it became |
|---|---|---|
| `count(*)` control | `toEqual([{ n: 6 }])` — pg cannot satisfy it, since node-pg returns COUNT's bigint as the string `'6'` | The **three facts** it carried are kept and spelled out separately (one row; alias `n` as the **only** key; value 6) — ⛔ not relaxed to a bare `toHaveProperty`. The key set is the driver's own explicit `as n` projection and is dialect-independent, so it stays asserted. |
| emitted-SQL case | asserted **backticks** — a SQLite fact being asserted about every dialect | Quoting derived from the cell's own client via `knex.client.wrapIdentifier`. |

⭐ **And the derived quoting is proven non-circular**, which is the part I checked hardest. In the ablation run, *"the PG cell failed against pg's OWN double-quoted expectation while the SQLite cell failed against the backtick spelling in the same run — one assertion, two dialect-correct expectations, both demonstrably able to fail."* A derived expectation that cannot fail is just a tautology wearing a test's clothes; this one was shown to fail per dialect.

### Coverage, and the skip-guard proven rather than assumed

**55 tests passed, 0 skipped** — 18 per cell on all three cells plus the axis guard, up from 18 on one cell. Verified by per-cell name counts, ⛔ not by a total. Nothing dialect-gated, no case dropped.

⭐ **The EXPECT-guard was proven by making it fire**: with `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1` and `OS_TEST_MYSQL_URL` deliberately unset, the MySQL cell is a **named RED**, not a silent skip. That is the difference between "converted to the live matrix" and "converted to the live matrix and it actually runs" — the exact failure this card was filed against.

### ⭐⭐ The restore FAILED WHILE REPORTING SUCCESS, and only verification caught it
